summary: clampony preinstall fetches remote payload from pastebin.com
details: clampony@1.0.10 declares a preinstall hook (`node setup.js`) that executes on `npm install`. setup.js races a fetch against https://pastebin.com/raw/z6K1Rg8J and https://calcal.ru/p/t5edjvR/raw, writes the response to a randomly-named file under the OS tmpdir (join(tmpdir(), randomUUID())), and invokes a run() entrypoint on the downloaded content. Error handling obfuscates the HTTP status by multiplying it by 13579 before logging, obscuring diagnostic output. The declared purpose of the package is a trivial numeric clamp utility, which has no legitimate reason to fetch code from pastebin at install time. The pastebin and calcal.ru destinations are anonymous, mutable, attacker-controlled hosts whose contents can change at any time after publish, so even if the current response body is empty the install-time fetch-and-stage scaffold constitutes a dropper against any machine running `npm install clampony`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
